headline: High: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API surfaces plus Kestra’s broad filesystem/network automation create dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflicts, and unverified downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes an MCP server and webhooks/APIs, while Kestra reads/writes files and runs declarative workflows that can ingest external content. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if OpenMetadata-delivered content is fed into Kestra tasks, though the profiles do not prove a default direct channel. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata webhook or MCP payloads are mapped into Kestra workflow inputs without sanitization, injection risk exists.
IF Kestra tasks parse OpenMetadata-produced text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer execution.
mitigations: Add strict allowlists for fields passed from OpenMetadata to Kestra.
Insert a manual approval step before Kestra executes any OpenMetadata-derived task.
Strip or escape instruction-like text from webhook/MCP payloads.
Use separate service accounts and isolated workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content-type validation end to end.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and can egress broadly. OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge via APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. If shared data flows between them, sensitive operational metadata can leak across the pair in default-style integrations; the profiles do not show hard isolation.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows forward logs, artifacts, or database data into OpenMetadata, those contents can be exposed in metadata systems.
IF OpenMetadata MCP/API responses are stored in Kestra artifacts or logs, sensitive lineage or governance data can leak.
mitigations: Disable forwarding of secrets and raw payloads into OpenMetadata.
Mask or redact Kestra logs before any export.
Restrict OpenMetadata API/MCP access to read-only metadata scopes.
Separate storage buckets and retention policies for workflow data and catalog data.
requires-engineering: implement field-level classification and redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra can write the filesystem, execute shells, spawn subprocesses, and request root/docker.sock, while OpenMetadata is runnable and exposes MCP/API-driven actions. Both support multiple instances, so concurrent writes to shared resources are plausible. Without explicit locking or isolation, overlapping mutable access can corrupt workflows or shared state; uncertainty does not justify downgrading.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, database, or git-backed config without locks, state corruption is possible.
IF OpenMetadata MCP actions and Kestra jobs mutate the same shared resource concurrently, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories and databases.
Disable concurrent writes to shared resources during coordinated runs.
Use advisory locks around any shared mutable target.
Run one agent read-only when the other is mutating shared state.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination or a job queue.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata’s governance/lineage outputs can become inputs to Kestra workflows, and Kestra can then execute shell, network, and cloud actions. That makes a classic cascade: one agent’s output can be treated as authoritative by the other and trigger downstream actions. Because Kestra has real execution authority, the blast radius is high even if the exact integration is not documented.
conditions: IF Kestra consumes OpenMetadata lineage or governance assertions without verification, incorrect metadata can drive wrong automation.
IF Kestra uses OpenMetadata outputs to trigger emails, cloud actions, or deployments, a bad upstream fact can cascade into real-world impact.
mitigations: Require human review for any OpenMetadata-derived automation trigger.
Add schema and freshness checks before Kestra acts on catalog data.
Compare OpenMetadata outputs against an independent source before execution.
Limit Kestra to dry-run mode for OpenMetadata-fed workflows.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and policy gates.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata is a governance/catalog system and Kestra processes logs, inputs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications. If regulated data classes are cataloged or moved between them, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR/DPA status, so I cannot claim a higher severity; uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated records are stored in Kestra artifacts and mirrored into OpenMetadata, retention and deletion obligations may diverge.
IF EU personal data is cataloged or transported through OpenMetadata and Kestra without a DPA or residency controls, compliance risk exists.
mitigations: Classify regulated fields before syncing between systems.
Exclude PHI/PII from catalog descriptions and lineage notes.
Set matching retention windows for workflow logs and metadata records.
Restrict cross-border transfers until legal review is complete.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and deletion propagation.
